cards.text: Psalm 95 opens with an invitation, and this psalm did NOT bring its indoor voice: "Come, let us sing for joy to the LORD; let us shout to the Rock of our salvation!" No polite humming in the back row, friend, we are SHOUTING.
And it keeps going: let us enter His presence with thanksgiving and make a joyful noise to Him in song. A joyful NOISE, friend, which is great news for me, because I sing like a squeaky oven door.

cards.question: All this singing and shouting has a reason. The psalm calls the LORD a great God. What else does it call Him?

answers.text: A great King above all gods
A great Judge of the earth

cards.text: Then the psalm shows how big this King is: the depths of the earth are in His hand, the mountain peaks belong to Him, and the sea is His. Meanwhile I spent years in ONE junk drawer, and I didn't even own THAT.

cards.question: The psalm says the sea belongs to the LORD because He ___ it.

cards.text: Then comes a second invitation to come, and the psalm calls the LORD our Maker. That's the One whose hands formed the dry land, friend, and my hands are a mustache that makes cookies on a good day.

cards.question: The psalm started with shouting and singing. Now how does it invite us to come before the LORD our Maker?
The psalm says the LORD is our God, and we are the people of His pasture, the ___ under His care.

cards.text: Then the whole mood flips, and a warning begins: "Today, if you hear His voice…" It's like a group chat full of party emojis, until somebody types, "Hey. Can we talk?"

cards.question: The warning begins, "Today, if you hear His voice…" What does the warning say not to do?

cards.text: The warning points back to Meribah and Massah, where the Israelites had no water, quarreled with Moses, Israel's leader, and tested the LORD by asking whether He was among them or not (Exodus 17:1-7). No water in the wilderness, friend, and a crowd turns into a complaint line FAST.
Now the voice in the psalm changes: God Himself starts speaking, and He says your fathers tested and tried Him there. When God starts talking, friend, I stand up STRAIGHT and fix my apron.

cards.question: When the fathers tested God, they had already seen His work.

cards.text: I can't point fingers, friend: I've watched my oven bake ten thousand perfect batches, and I STILL crack the door every two minutes to check on it. Then God says that for forty years He was angry with that generation.

cards.question: God was angry for forty years with the generation that tested Him in the wilderness. What does He say about their hearts?
God says the generation that tested Him in the wilderness had known His ways.

cards.text: So God swore an oath in His anger about that generation. I think this is the hardest line in the whole psalm.

cards.question: What did God swear in His anger about the generation that tested Him in the wilderness?

answers.text: They will never enter His rest
They will never see His face
They will never build His house
